JUSTICE S.VISHWAJITH SHETTY) Accused Nos.1 and 2 are before this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C with the prayer to quash the entire proceedings in PCR No.108/2024 pending before the Court of III Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Kalaburgi and FIR in Crime No.73/2024 registered by Chowk Police Station, NC: 2025:KHC-K:139 Kalaburagi City for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 504 and 506 of IPC.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3.

The respondent No.2 herein has filed a private complaint before the Jurisdictional Magistrate in P.C.No.108/2024, which was referred by the Jurisdictional Magistrate to the police for investigation Sagar Dubey And Anr vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93453351/
2 under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C and in turn the Chowk Police Station, Kalaburagi have registered FIR in Crime No.73/2024 against petitioner herein and another for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 504 and 506 of IPC.
4.

sentences.text:
Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioners herein, who are arrayed as accused Nos.1 and 2 in Crime No.73/2024 are before this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
5.

Learned counsel for the petitioners having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that accused No.1 has initiated 138 proceedings as against the NC: 2025:KHC-K:139 husband of the respondent herein and as a counter to the same, the present complaint has been filed.

He submits that there is an inordinate delay in filing the private complaint and no reply was given to the statutory notice issued on behalf of accused No.1 in the proceedings under Section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act.
Only to harass the petitioners a false criminal case has been registered.
6. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader and learned counsel for respondent No.2 have opposed petition.

Respondent No.2 submits that on the pretext of availing loan from a private finance company, accused persons have taken the blank signed cheques of respondent No.2 and on the basis of the said blank cheques accused Nos.1 and 3 have already initiated proceedings for offence punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.
In the event the criminal proceedings are quashed, the defence of the respondent No.2 in the proceedings under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act is likely to be prejudiced.
Police have NC: 2025:KHC-K:139 registered an FIR against accused persons and if the investigation is intercepted the same is likely to cause serious injustice to respondent No.2.
Accordingly, pray to dismiss the petition.

7. Perusal of the private complaint filed by the respondent No.2 would reveal that it is her specific case that accused Nos.1 to 3, who had collected three signed cheques from her and her husband on the pretext of availing financial facility from Bajaj Finance, Kalbargi had not provided any financial facility to them and on the other hand the three cheques, which were taken by them was misused and they have refused to return the cheques in spite of demand made by them.

In the private complaint it is stated that respondent No.2 had approached the police and necessary endorsement to the said defect is also produced before the Jurisdictional Magistrate along with the private Complaint.

It cannot be said that there is absolutely no merit in the allegations found in the first information and respondent No.2 has complied the NC: 2025:KHC-K:139 requirement of law prior to she filing a private complaint before the Jurisdictional Magistrate.

Therefore, it cannot be said that the Jurisdictional Magistrate has erred in referring the private complaint to the Jurisdictional police under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. for the purpose of investigation.

Merely for the reason that respondent No.2 had not replied to the statutory notice issued to her under Section 138 of the Negotiation Instruments Act, the same cannot be a ground to quash the impugned criminal proceedings at this stage when the matter is still under the investigation by the police.
8. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of SKODA AUTO VOLKSWAGEN (INDIA) Vs. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH AND OTHERS reported in (2021) 5 SCC 795 and in the case of M/s.

PVT. LTD. Vs. STATE OF MAHARASHTRA AND OTHERS reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 315, has observed that the powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C Sagar Dubey And Anr vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93453351/
3 should not be normally exercised to NC: 2025:KHC-K:139 scuttle the investigation by the police and the High Court should be slow while exercising their inherent powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C wherein a prayer is made to interfere with the investigation by the police.
